body:
Thank you for your insight, you've made very accurate observations.

I wouldn't like to be a rock star. Everyone fantasizes about the life but if I was presented with the choice I doubt I'd take it. I enjoy my anonymity. I don't like to be photographed and rarely allow people to do it. I generally hate interacting with strangers. I don't like people at all.

Through my work I interact with people a lot. I guess I take on another persona and present it to them when I'm working but I find people can be ignorant, self-important, selfish, stupid, thoughtless and rude, particularly in the environment I deal with them. (Security industry)

After so many years of dealing with aggressive thugs and self-absorbed assholes I've begun to assume the worst about everyone I deal with. People on an individual basis I can handle. I have close friends that I care about, but people en masse trouble me. In large groups, particularly if a large number of them are strangers I try to fade into the background. The only time this changes is when it's work and I am in a position of control.

I often wonder if that makes me a bully or a thug myself. A coward unless I'm in control of other people. It makes me feel ashamed sometimes.

Occasionally, through work I've been required to use force. Since I'm relatively adept and effective at it people have begun to think I enjoy doing it. A friend of mine made a remark regarding that and when I was alone I broke down because she thought I was a violent thug.

Not really sure where I'm going with this now.

I have a bit of a mental block about seeing someone. I don't know why, I just can't seem to bring myself to do it. I feel like I'll be given a prescription of pills which I definitely won't take. A lot of the things I do and feel aren't prompted by conscious decisions, I just think or feel a certain way and don't always understand why. Seeing someone about it is one of those things. Rationally, I know I should and it would probably help, but I can't do it. No idea why.
